narrative:
The model estimated a 51.0% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is only slightly above even odds, so this is not a prediction of certain failure; it means the estimated risk crossed the school’s decision threshold and your application was denied.

The denial was driven mainly by your third-year class-rank decile, the most influential factor. Your decile was 1, far below the average of 5.79 among accepted students, and this pushed the prediction strongly toward bar-exam failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.20 was close to the accepted-student average of 3.23; this factor was the second most important and actually pushed toward passing. Your middle family-income bracket was the third most important factor and also pushed slightly toward passing, since middle-income students make up a substantial share of accepted applicants, though upper-middle income was more common. Those favorable signals were not enough to offset the much stronger concern about your third-year academic standing.

Next, ask admissions for specific feedback, focus on strengthening your upper-level academic record, and consider retaking the LSAT and using bar-readiness preparation to show improved readiness. Reapply after you can document stronger academic performance and a more competitive application.
